title: Same badge twice

idea.rule: Check every name against ALL the names before it, not just the one next door.
idea.detail: A set remembers everyone you've seen so far, and 'name in seen' asks it in one step. Walk the list once: if the name is already in the set, that's a repeat; otherwise add it. A repeat can be anywhere earlier — not just right next door.

watch.code:
dup = False
seen = set()
for name in log:
    if name in seen:
        dup = True
    seen.add(name)
print(dup)

model_restatement: Say True if any name appears more than once, otherwise False.

clarify.question: Could the same person be spelled differently?
clarify.answer: No — names are clean and lowercase today.

clarify.question: Do you want who signed in twice?
What if the list is empty or has one name?
clarify.answer: Then nobody signed in twice — False.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Go down the sign-in sheet comparing each name with the next one. If they match, someone signed in twice. Print the answer.

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 3 is the last comparison. What is i?
With the fix — iteration 4 (the second ana): after line 5, what is dup?

why_line: Comparing only neighbours checks ana–ben, ben–cy, cy–ana. The two anas are three seats apart, so no neighbour pair ever matches.

explain.rule: Checking only the next seat is a bouncer who remembers one face — the second ana walks in three people later and he's forgotten her.
explain.bridge: So what could remember EVERY name you've seen so far?

fix.rule: A set remembers every name so far; 'name in seen' checks all of them at once.

walk.gloss: Have we seen this name anywhere before?

fix.recommended:
dup = False
seen = set()
for name in names:
    if name in seen:
        dup = True
    seen.add(name)
print(dup)

alternatives.note: A set drops repeats, so it's shorter if there was one — the shortcut.
